title: cmd/link: windows/arm64 internal linking rejects Clang COFF NODUPLICATES and ASSOCIATIVE sections

labels.name: compiler/runtime
labels.description: Issues related to the Go compiler and/or runtime.

body:
### Go version

`go version go1.27.1 darwin/arm64` (Homebrew)

Clang 23.1.0, targeting `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`.

### Output of `go env` in your module/workspace:

Relevant values under the reproduction command below:

```text
GO111MODULE='off'
GOARCH='arm64'
GOARM64='v8.0'
GOHOSTARCH='arm64'
GOHOSTOS='darwin'
GOOS='windows'
GOEXE='.exe'
GOEXPERIMENT=''
GOFLAGS=''
GOFIPS140='off'
GOTOOLCHAIN='local'
GOVERSION='go1.27.1'
GOWORK='off'
CGO_ENABLED='0'
```

`GOENV=off` disables saved Go configuration. Clang is invoked separately, so
the reduction does not need a Windows SDK or a configured CGo environment.

### What did you do?

Reduced an internal-link failure seen while testing native Windows ARM64 CGo
with MSVC-target Clang in
https://github.com/conda-forge/go-feedstock/pull/339.
The following reduction uses the stock Go toolchain, without the feedstock's
patches, and can be cross-linked from macOS ARM64.

Create this layout:

```text
repro/
  functions.c
  smoke/
    main.go
```

`functions.c`:

```c
__declspec(noinline) int repro_leaf(int n) { return n + 1; }

__declspec(noinline) int repro_nonleaf(int n) {
    return repro_leaf(n) + 1;
}
```

`smoke/main.go`:

```go
package main

func main() {}
```

From `repro/`, using Clang and llvm-readobj 23.1.0:

```sh
clang --target=aarch64-pc-windows-msvc -O2 -ffunction-sections \
  -c functions.c -o smoke/repro_windows_arm64.syso
llvm-readobj --symbols --relocations --unwind smoke/repro_windows_arm64.syso
cd smoke
GOENV=off GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOWORK=off \
  GOOS=windows GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 GO111MODULE=off \
  go build -ldflags=-linkmode=internal -o repro.exe .
```

### What did you see happen?

The stock linker exits with status 1:

```text
internal error: unsupported COMDAT selection strategy found in path=<archive>(repro_windows_ar) sec=4 strategy=1 idx=6, please file a bug
```

The input contains NODUPLICATES (1) `.text` sections for the two functions.
The non-leaf function also has ASSOCIATIVE (5) `.xdata` and `.pdata` sections,
both referring to its `.text` section. Its `.pdata` record is eight bytes,
with packed unwind information and an ARM64_ADDR32NB relocation.

A separate diagnostic linker with the feedstock's NODUPLICATES support patch
(including duplicate-definition checking) reaches the next error:

```text
internal error: unsupported COMDAT selection strategy found in path=<archive>(repro_windows_ar) sec=5 strategy=5 idx=12, please file a bug
```

That second result is from the modified diagnostic linker, not stock Go.
The stock reproduction above stops at strategy 1.

At inspected master commit
[`714d9afb66994e987aa715e088279e75efcec315`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/714d9afb66994e987aa715e088279e75efcec315/src/cmd/link/internal/loadpe/ldpe.go#L791),
the loader still accepts only ANY and SAME_SIZE. I have not built and run tip.

### What did you expect to see?

Support for internally linking these MSVC-target Clang COFF sections, or
guidance on whether this object form is intentionally outside the supported
internal-linker subset. This is a missing-capability report, not a claim of a
regression from an earlier release.

Related work: Windows ARM64 internal linking landed in
https://github.com/golang/go/issues/75485, MSVC-target Clang support in
https://go.dev/cl/703055, and the existing COMDAT selection support in
https://go.dev/cl/383835.

Related ARM64 SEH work is discussed in
https://github.com/golang/go/issues/57302. Preserving existing C-host unwind
data is another limitation, so simply accepting strategy 5 would not establish
correct unwind handling. This report is about section loading and association,
not generating unwind metadata for Go frames.

Would a scoped change for NODUPLICATES and its associative children be a useful
first step, or is there existing work to coordinate with?

title: cmd/go: go test std should give a clearer error with GO111MODULE=off

labels.name: NeedsInvestigation
labels.description: Someone must examine and confirm this is a valid issue and not a duplicate of an existing one.

labels.name: BadErrorMessage
labels.description: Issues related compiler error messages that should be better.

body:
### Go version

go version go1.27.1 darwin/arm64

### What did you do?

Prior to filing this issue, I forgot that it was already decided and documented that testing the Go standard library with GO111MODULE=auto or GO111MODULE=off is not supported (see `go help gopath` and issue #69202). Consider what happens if someone attempts to do it anyway:

```shell
$ go test net/http
$ GO111MODULE=off go test net/http
```

### What did you see happen?

```shell
$ go test net/http
ok  	net/http	13.379s
$ GO111MODULE=off go test net/http
< 3186407 bytes of output, which are unhelpful as testing standard library packages
  with GO111MODULE111=off is unsupported and known to produce false positive signal >
```

### What did you expect to see?

```shell
$ go test net/http
ok  	net/http	13.379s
$ GO111MODULE=off go test net/http
go: modules disabled by GO111MODULE=off; see 'go help gopath'
```

Or some better phrasing - see related issue #66080 about `go get` error clarity.

Implementing this might be tricky since it'd have to be done without also breaking the ability for `cmd/go` tests themselves to test this mode (given proposal #60915), but if it can be done somehow it may reduce possibility of confusion in the future.

CC @matloob (via https://dev.golang.org/owners).

title: x/build/internal/gcsfs: handle explicit GCS folders

labels.name: NeedsFix
labels.description: The path to resolution is known, but the work has not been done.

body:
When working with GCS, one can end up with folders that are either implicit (aka "simulated"?) or explicit (aka "zero-byte object whose name ends with a trailing / delimiter"). Currently the gcsfs.NewFS implementation assumes all folders are implicit, and in practice that's the only input relui currently provides. However, while working on #81345 I found out that explicit folders aren't handled properly, and this limitation isn't documented.

It manifests as NewFS(...).ReadDir returning an extra entry with a name that doesn't exist (usually the parent folder name). It can also be caught with testing/fstest.Test provided NewFS(...) is given a GCS bucket with explicit folders.

Filing this so that this finding isn't lost, but there's no need to resolve this soon since this is an internal package and it's not a problem for its current uses.

CC @golang/release.

labels.name: NeedsInvestigation

body:
gotip-linux-ppc64_power10 builders are consistently failing, almost always with an infra failure that looks like the test runner is killed before it runs any tests.

e.g., https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/golang/builders/ci/gotip-linux-ppc64_power10/b8671984145164140817/infra

```
[I2026-08-31T03:54:58.777198Z 971126 0 cmd_stream.go:577] rdb-stream: starting the test command - ["/home/swarming/.swarming/w/ir/cache/tools/bin/result_adapter" "go" "-v=false" "-dump-json" "/home/swarming/.swarming/w/ir/x/w/dist.testjson" "--" "/home/swarming/.swarming/w/ir/x/w/goroot/bin/go" "tool" "dist" "test" "-json"]
[W2026-08-31T04:05:27.357411Z 971126 0 cmd_stream.go:589] rdb-stream: test process exited with error: signal: killed
```

Sometimes they get far enough for tests to fail: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/golang/builders/ci/gotip-linux-ppc64_power10/b8671812430834306609/overview

The bots don't seem completely broken, as x repo builds seem to work OK.

The dashboard shows the first failing CL as https://go.dev/cl/817160, but I'm not sure if that is related or this is an infra problem that occurred at the same time.

cc @golang/ppc64 @matloob
